newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Western world nickel production up in May - INSG.
newsitem.headline: Western world nickel production up in May - INSG.

text.p: Western world production of primary nickel rose to 60,000 tonnes in May from 58,100 in April, the International Nickel Study Group said.

Canada raised its output by 400 tonnes to 12,500 and U.S. production returned to a more normal level of 1,400 tonnes after dipping in April to 700. Colombian output increased to 2,000 tonnes from 1,100.
The total for New Caledonia was up 300 tonnes to 4,200.
But these rises were countered by weak European figures. Finnish production dropped 300 tonnes to 3,500, French was down 200 tonnes at 1,000 and Norwegian fell to 5,600 from 6,100.

Nickel mine production in the west was relatively steady at 61,100 tonnes in May against 61,700 in April. But the flat total masked strong American and Asian numbers undermined by weak output from New Caledonia.
Production in Canada, the world's biggest miner, was up at 19,000 tonnes from 18,300 and Colombia's was 2,500 from 1,400. Indonesian output rose to 7,000 from 5,500 tonnes.
But these rises were countered by a sharp drop in output from New Caledonia, which fell to 9,200 tonnes from an usually high total of 13,800 tonnes in April.
Western world nickel consumption was little changed in May at 75,900 tonnes against 75,600 in April.
